findings.summary: The seal-verified Implement verification record still accepts any `systemctl --user is-system-running` exit code of 0 or 1 without checking that the raw state is `running` or `degraded`, so a connection error (which also exits 1) can pass acceptance; the corrected `deploy/verify-user-session-bus.sh` helper that enforces the connected-manager state is never invoked by the record.

The Implement verification record stores only argv, exit codes, and test counts and still omits the captured UTC timestamps and the raw `systemctl --user is-system-running` and `make verify` output required as acceptance evidence by the spec.
